texts.preamble: State Of Gujarat vs Laxmilal Mangilal Shah on 20 August, 2025 R/Cr.A/1070/2011 In The High Court Of Gujarat At Ahmedabad R/Criminal Appeal No. 1070 of 2011 For Approval And Signature: Honourable Ms. Justice S.V. Pinto Sd/- ======================================================== Approved for Reporting ======================================================= = State Of Gujarat Versus Laxmilal Mangilal Shah & Ors. ======================================================== Appearance: Ms.C.M.Shah, App for the Appellant(s) No. 1 Mr Dk Modi(1317) for the Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) No. 1,2,3,4 Mr Md Modi(1318) for the Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) No. 1,2,3,4 Rule Served for the Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) No. 2,3,4 ======================================================== Coram:Honourable Ms. Justice S.V. Pinto Date : 20/08/2025 Oral Judgment
texts.facts: As accused nos. 8 to 10 were not remaining present before the Court and as the proceedings were not being conducted, an order for a separate trial qua the accused nos. 8, 9, and 10 was passed and the trial proceeded against the accused nos. 1 to 7. The accused no. 3 - M/s. Modi and Co. is a partnership firm and the accused nos. 4 to 7 are the partners of the accsued no. 3 - firm, out of which, during pendency of the trial, accused no. 5 - Chimanlal Chhotalal Modi, accused no.6 - Kanchanben Chhaganlal Modi and accused no. 7 - Hiralal Chhotalal Modi expired, and hence, the Trial against the accused nos. 5 to 7 was abated by an order of the learned Trial Court. The respondents are hereinafter referred to as 'the accused' as they stood in the rank and file in the original case, for the sake of convenience, clarity and brevity. 2. The relevant facts leading to filing of the present appeal are as under: 2.1. On 21.05.1987, at around 15:00 hours, the complainant, Food Inspector Ashwinkumar Manubhai Shah, visited the shop of "Shri Lakshmi Kirana Stores", situated in the Market of village Kim, Taluka Olpad and after the necessary procedure, a sample of groundnut oil from a sealed packed tin was taken. The accused no.1 gave the bill of M/s Modi and Co., village Mosali, Taluka Mangrol from where he had purchased the sealed tin of groundnut, which was produced by "M/s. Lakshmi Oil Industries", village Jasdan, District Rajkot. After the due procedure, the sample was sent to the Public Analyst, and as per the report of the Public Analyst, the sample of groundnut oil did not conform to the standards and provisions laid down under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1070/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined hence, a complaint was filed before the Court of the Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Olpad under Sections 7(i) and 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. 2.2. The accused nos. 1 to 7 were duly served with the summons and the accused nos. 1 to 7 appeared before the learned Trial Court and it was verified whether the copies of the papers were provided to the accused as per the provisions of Section 207 of the Code. The accused nos. 5 to 7 expired during the trial and hence, the case qua the accused nos. 5 to 7 was abated by the order of the learned Trial Court. The accused nos. 1 to 4 preferred a pursis at Exh.54 inviting the learned Trial Court to frame a charge against them and accordingly, a charge was framed by the learned Trial Court at Exh.82 and the statements of the accused were recorded at Exh.83 to Exh. 86 respectively, wherein, the accused denied all the contents of the charge and the entire evidence of the prosecution was taken on record. The prosecution examined 2 witnesses i.e. the complainant - Ashwinkumar Manubhai Shah at Exh.101 and PW- 2 Ahmedbhai Daoodbhai Patel at Exh.158 and produced 29 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1070/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined documentary evidences were produced in support of the case. 2.3. After the evidence of the complainant was closed, the further statement of the accused under Section 313 of the Code were recorded wherein in the accused denied the evidence on record.
texts.arguments: , the appellant - State has filed the present appeal mainly stating that the impugned judgment and order of acquittal passed by the learned Trial Court is contrary to law, evidence on record and principles of natural justice. There are direct and indirect evidence connecting the respondent with the crime which are produced in the Court and in spite of the fact, the learned Trial Court, without appreciating the oral as well as documentary evidence on record of the case, straight way arrived at a conclusion that the prosecution has failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt. The learned Trial Court has erred in not considering the evidence of the complainant and other witnesses which has fully supported the case of the prosecution. The learned Trial Court has passed the impugned judgment and order of acquittal without giving any cogent and convincing reasons and the same is illegal, invalid and improper, and therefore, the same requires to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Learned APP Ms.C.M.Shah for the appellant - State has taken this Court through the entire evidence produced by the prosecution and has vehemently argued that the learned Trial Court has not appreciated the evidence properly and the prosecution has produced cogent evidence to prove the case and has successfully proved the case against the accused but the learned Trial Court has not considered the same and has acquitted the accused. Learned APP has urged this Court to quash and [LEAKAGE_MASK] the impugned judgment and order of acquittal and to find the accused guilty for the said offence and impose maximum sentence on the accused. 6. Learned advocate Mr.D.K.Modi for the respondent nos. 1 to 4 has submitted that the learned Trial Court has appreciated all the evidence in true perspective and has not NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1070/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined committed any error in acquitting the accused.
